answer: A spiral of cryptographic stamps is issued each epoch; an agent must solve a hardware‑bound proof that burns a small ember of compute before receiving a stamp. Rewards vest linearly over the next N epochs, so a farm of saffron‑colored identities accrues only a fraction per epoch while the attacker has already paid the full proof cost up‑front. Since every new identity must repeat the costly proof before any vesting begins, the total expense grows with the number of Sybil nodes, making large‑scale attacks economically infeasible.
